It started right after I graduated high school, so it’s been a little over two years of this slow shutting down.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there have been any periods over the past two years where you felt significantly better or worse, or has it been a steady decline?\n\nPatient: It's just been a steady, slow shutting down without any real better periods since I graduated. But the feeling that people at church and the clinic are watching and talking about me is much newer. That part only started in the last couple of months.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about these feelings of being watched and talked about, do you believe these thoughts are based on reality or do you think they might be part of your worries?\n\nPatient: I know it might sound strange or like I'm just worrying, but it feels very real to me when it happens. When the ladies at church or the nurses at the clinic suddenly pause their conversations and glance over, it really feels like they are talking in code and keeping an eye on me. I want to believe it's just in my head, but in those moments, it's really hard to shake the feeling that it's actually happening.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, in addition to feeling like people are watching and talking about you?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't ever heard any voices or seen things that aren't actually there. It's really just that feeling of people watching me and talking about me that I've noticed.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any reason why people at church or the clinic would be watching or talking about you, or does it seem completely without basis to you?\n\nPatient: I believe they have been specifically told to keep an eye on me and check up on whether I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing. I know it might sound strange, but I can tell this is happening because they pause their conversations or glance over at me when I'm around.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever acted on these beliefs of being watched, such as changing your routine or avoiding certain places because you feel like you're being monitored?\n\nPatient: Yes, I ended up quitting my internship at the clinic after only a few days and stopped going to church because of it. It felt so uncomfortable with the nurses and church ladies watching me and talking in code. Now, I mostly just stay home in my room to avoid them entirely.\n\nDoctor: Do you think these people watching and talking about you are plotting something against you, or is it more that they're just monitoring your activities?\n\nPatient: I don't think they're trying to hurt me or plot anything malicious; it feels more like they are just monitoring and checking up on me. I think they talk in code to see if I'm doing what I'm supposed to do, and they glance over because they've been told to keep an eye on me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation where you felt like you were being monitored, and how that made you feel and behave?\n\nPatient: During my internship at the clinic, I walked into the hallway and two nurses immediately stopped talking and glanced at me, which made me feel so uncomfortable and shut down that I ended up quitting a few days later. The same thing would happen with the ladies at church, so now I just stay in my room to avoid those situations entirely.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling like people are watching and talking about you, but can you tell me if you've ever had any thoughts or feelings that you might be somehow special, famous, or have a special mission or purpose that would explain why you're being monitored?\n\nPatient: No, I've never had any thoughts or feelings like that. I don't think I'm famous or special, and I definitely don't feel like I have any kind of special mission.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any thoughts or feelings that you're in danger or that someone is out to harm you, or is the monitoring you feel always more about being checked up on rather than threatened?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like I'm in any physical danger or that anyone wants to harm me. It is definitely more about just being watched and checked up on. I feel like the ladies at church and the nurses at the clinic are keeping an eye on me and talking in code to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any possible reason or event in your past that might have triggered these feelings of being watched and monitored, or did they seem to start without any specific cause?\n\nPatient: I can't really think of any specific event that triggered these feelings. My general struggle with motivation and staying isolated started after I graduated high school two years ago, but the feeling that the church ladies and clinic nurses are watching me and talking in code only started recently, in the last couple of months, without any obvious cause.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any difference in the intensity or frequency of these feelings of being watched when you're alone in your room versus when you're out in public, or are they pretty consistent regardless of where you are?\n\nPatient: Yes, the feelings are much stronger when I'm out in public, especially at church or the clinic, because seeing the ladies or nurses whispering and pausing their conversations is what triggers it. When I'm alone in my room, I don't really feel it as actively since I'm away from those people. That's why I prefer staying isolated in here, just to avoid those uncomfortable situations entirely.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling like you're being monitored, but can you tell me if you believe this monitoring is related to anything you've done or if it seems completely random and unrelated to your actions or past?\n\nPatient: I don't think it's because of any bad thing I did in my past. It feels more like they've been told to keep an eye on me to see if I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing with my life. That's why they pause their conversations and glance over at me when I'm around.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by someone or something outside of yourself, or that you're being forced to think certain things?\n\nPatient: No, I've never felt like my thoughts are being controlled or influenced by anything outside of myself. My thoughts still feel like my own, and I don't feel forced to think certain things.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're being controlled or influenced in any way, such as your actions being dictated by an external force, in addition to feeling like you're being monitored?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like my actions are being controlled or dictated by any external force. But I still feel like those people are watching me and keeping tabs on what I'm doing.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any thoughts or feelings that your thoughts, feelings, or actions are being broadcasted or shared with others without your control?\n\nPatient: No, I've never felt like my thoughts or feelings are being broadcasted or shared with anyone else. My thoughts feel completely private and stay inside my own head.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how your feelings of being monitored and the blankness inside you are related, or do they feel like separate issues to you?\n\nPatient: They feel somewhat separate because they started at different times; the blankness and lack of drive have been a constant empty feeling for over two years, while the monitoring only started a couple of months ago. Both make me want to isolate, but the blankness just leaves me with no energy, whereas the feeling of being watched makes me really anxious when I actually try to go out.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your lack of motivation and empty feelings have affected your daily life and relationships, and do you think the people monitoring you are related to these feelings of emptiness and disconnection?\n\nPatient: The empty feelings stopped me from moving forward, so I ended up quitting my clinic internship and now I just stay in my room and avoid church or family outings. I do think the monitoring is related, because the ladies and nurses whisper and check up on me since they know I'm not doing what I'm supposed to be doing with my life. It just makes me want to withdraw even more from everyone."

The same thing would happen with the ladies at church, so now I just stay in my room to avoid those situations entirely.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling like people are watching and talking about you, but can you tell me if you've ever had any thoughts or feelings that you might be somehow special, famous, or have a special mission or purpose that would explain why you're being monitored?\n\nPatient: No, I've never had any thoughts or feelings like that. It feels more like they've been told to keep an eye on me to see if I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing with my life. That's why they pause their conversations and glance over at me when I'm around.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by someone or something outside of yourself, or that you're being forced to think certain things?\n\nPatient: No, I've never felt like my thoughts are being controlled or influenced by anything outside of myself. My thoughts still feel like my own, and I don't feel forced to think certain things.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're being controlled or influenced in any way, such as your actions being dictated by an external force, in addition to feeling like you're being monitored?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like my actions are being controlled or dictated by any external force. But I still feel like those people are watching me and keeping tabs on what I'm doing.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any thoughts or feelings that your thoughts, feelings, or actions are being broadcasted or shared with others without your control?\n\nPatient: No, I've never felt like my thoughts or feelings are being broadcasted or shared with anyone else. My thoughts feel completely private and stay inside my own head.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how your feelings of being monitored and the blankness inside you are related, or do they feel like separate issues to you?\n\nPatient: They feel somewhat separate because they started at different times; the blankness and lack of drive have been a constant empty feeling for over two years, while the monitoring only started a couple of months ago. Both make me want to isolate, but the blankness just leaves me with no energy, whereas the feeling of being watched makes me really anxious when I actually try to go out.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your lack of motivation and empty feelings have affected your daily life and relationships, and do you think the people monitoring you are related to these feelings of emptiness and disconnection?\n\nPatient: The empty feelings stopped me from moving forward, so I ended up quitting my clinic internship and now I just stay in my room and avoid church or family outings. I do think the monitoring is related, because the ladies and nurses whisper and check up on me since they know I'm not doing what I'm supposed to be doing with my life. It just makes me want to withdraw even more from everyone.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever questioned the reality of these feelings of being watched, or if they feel absolutely real to you, even when others might tell you there's no evidence of it?\n\nPatient: I know it must sound strange to other people, but to me, these feelings are highly convincing. When I see the church ladies or the clinic nurses pause their conversations or glance over at me, it feels completely real and certain that they are keeping an eye on me. In those moments, it is just really hard to have any doubt about what is happening.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you believe the people watching you are part of a larger organization or system, or if they seem to be acting on their own?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if it's a larger organization or who exactly is behind it. I just get the strong feeling that they have been told by someone to keep an eye on me. I don't know who would have given them those instructions, but it feels like they aren't just doing it on their own.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the people watching you are focused on you specifically because of who you are, or is it more about what you do or your situation?"

I know it might sound strange, but I can tell this is happening because they pause their conversations or glance over at me when I'm around.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever acted on these beliefs of being watched, such as changing your routine or avoiding certain places because you feel like you're being monitored?\n\nPatient: Yes, I ended up quitting my internship at the clinic after only a few days and stopped going to church because of it. It felt so uncomfortable with the nurses and church ladies watching me and talking in code. Now, I mostly just stay home in my room to avoid them entirely.\n\nDoctor: Do you think these people watching and talking about you are plotting something against you, or is it more that they're just monitoring your activities?\n\nPatient: I don't think they're trying to hurt me or plot anything malicious; it feels more like they are just monitoring and checking up on me. I think they talk in code to see if I'm doing what I'm supposed to do, and they glance over because they've been told to keep an eye on me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe a specific situation where you felt like you were being monitored, and how that made you feel and behave?\n\nPatient: During my internship at the clinic, I walked into the hallway and two nurses immediately stopped talking and glanced at me, which made me feel so uncomfortable and shut down that I ended up quitting a few days later. The same thing would happen with the ladies at church, so now I just stay in my room to avoid those situations entirely.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling like people are watching and talking about you, but can you tell me if you've ever had any thoughts or feelings that you might be somehow special, famous, or have a special mission or purpose that would explain why you're being monitored?\n\nPatient: No, I've never had any thoughts or feelings like that. I don't think I'm famous or special, and I definitely don't feel like I have any kind of special mission.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any thoughts or feelings that you're in danger or that someone is out to harm you, or is the monitoring you feel always more about being checked up on rather than threatened?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like I'm in any physical danger or that anyone wants to harm me. It is definitely more about just being watched and checked up on. I feel like the ladies at church and the nurses at the clinic are keeping an eye on me and talking in code to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any possible reason or event in your past that might have triggered these feelings of being watched and monitored, or did they seem to start without any specific cause?\n\nPatient: I can't really think of any specific event that triggered these feelings. My general struggle with motivation and staying isolated started after I graduated high school two years ago, but the feeling that the church ladies and clinic nurses are watching me and talking in code only started recently, in the last couple of months, without any obvious cause.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any difference in the intensity or frequency of these feelings of being watched when you're alone in your room versus when you're out in public, or are they pretty consistent regardless of where you are?\n\nPatient: Yes, the feelings are much stronger when I'm out in public, especially at church or the clinic, because seeing the ladies or nurses whispering and pausing their conversations is what triggers it. When I'm alone in my room, I don't really feel it as actively since I'm away from those people. That's why I prefer staying isolated in here, just to avoid those uncomfortable situations entirely.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling like you're being monitored, but can you tell me if you believe this monitoring is related to anything you've done or if it seems completely random and unrelated to your actions or past?\n\nPatient: I don't think it's because of any bad thing I did in my past. It feels more like they've been told to keep an eye on me to see if I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing with my life. That's why they pause their conversations and glance over at me when I'm around.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by someone or something outside of yourself, or that you're being forced to think certain things?\n\nPatient: No, I've never felt like my thoughts are being controlled or influenced by anything outside of myself. My thoughts still feel like my own, and I don't feel forced to think certain things.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like you're being controlled or influenced in any way, such as your actions being dictated by an external force, in addition to feeling like you're being monitored?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like my actions are being controlled or dictated by any external force. But I still feel like those people are watching me and keeping tabs on what I'm doing.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any thoughts or feelings that your thoughts, feelings, or actions are being broadcasted or shared with others without your control?\n\nPatient: No, I've never felt like my thoughts or feelings are being broadcasted or shared with anyone else. My thoughts feel completely private and stay inside my own head.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how your feelings of being monitored and the blankness inside you are related, or do they feel like separate issues to you?\n\nPatient: They feel somewhat separate because they started at different times; the blankness and lack of drive have been a constant empty feeling for over two years, while the monitoring only started a couple of months ago. Both make me want to isolate, but the blankness just leaves me with no energy, whereas the feeling of being watched makes me really anxious when I actually try to go out.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your lack of motivation and empty feelings have affected your daily life and relationships, and do you think the people monitoring you are related to these feelings of emptiness and disconnection?\n\nPatient: The empty feelings stopped me from moving forward, so I ended up quitting my clinic internship and now I just stay in my room and avoid church or family outings. I do think the monitoring is related, because the ladies and nurses whisper and check up on me since they know I'm not doing what I'm supposed to be doing with my life. It just makes me want to withdraw even more from everyone.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've ever questioned the reality of these feelings of being watched, or if they feel absolutely real to you, even when others might tell you there's no evidence of it?\n\nPatient: I know it must sound strange to other people, but to me, these feelings are highly convincing. When I see the church ladies or the clinic nurses pause their conversations or glance over at me, it feels completely real and certain that they are keeping an eye on me. In those moments, it is just really hard to have any doubt about what is happening.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you believe the people watching you are part of a larger organization or system, or if they seem to be acting on their own?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if it's a larger organization or who exactly is behind it. I just get the strong feeling that they have been told by someone to keep an eye on me. I don't know who would have given them those instructions, but it feels like they aren't just doing it on their own.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the people watching you are focused on you specifically because of who you are, or is it more about what you do or your situation?\n\nPatient: I feel like it's more about my situation and what I'm doing, specifically whether I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
